questions.question: Which of the following types of agriculture is known as Jhum in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shifting Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shifting Agriculture**

 
 
• Under Shifting cultivation, a piece of land is used for quite some years until the fertility is dropped. After that, the farmers move to the new plots. It is practiced by tribal and is also known as Burn and Slash cultivation.
 
• It is known as Jhoom in Assam, Bewar in Madhya Pradesh, Onam in Kerala, Podu in Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha.
 
• 
 
Over a large part of North East India shifting cultivation used, while having different local names are found to be the same-named as Jhoom cultivation. Jhoom cultivation, also known as Slash-and-Burn cultivation.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Other Names of Shifting Cultivation:

__
 
• Shifting Cultivation is known as Ladang in Indonesia,__
 
• Caingin in the Philippines,
 
• Milpa in Central America & Mexico,
 
• Ray in Vietnam,
 
• Taungya in Myanmar,
 
• Tamrai in Thailand,
 
• __Chena in Sri Lanka,__
 
• Conuco in Venezuela,
 
• Roca in Brazil,
 
• Masole in central Africa.

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojna was introduced in 2015 under the ______.

options.text: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)
 
• Launch
 
 
• India’s largest Skill Certification Scheme - Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) - was launched on 15th July 2015 (World Youth Skills Day).
 
 
 
• Aim
 
 
• To encourage and promote skill development in the country by providing free short-duration skill training and incentivizing this by providing monetary rewards to youth for skill certification.
 
 
 
• Implementation
 
 
• PMKVY is implemented by the National Skills Development Corporation (NSDC) under the guidance of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE).
 
 
 
• ​Features:
 
 
• It envisages training of eight lakh candidates over a scheme period of 2020-2021 with an outlay of Rs. 948.90 crore.
 
• The 729 Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs), impaneled non-PMKK training centers and more than 200 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under Skill India will be rolling out PMKVY 3.0 training to build a robust pool of skilled professionals.
 
• It will be more trainee- and learner-centric. The focus is on bridging the demand-supply gap by promoting skill development in areas of new-age and Industry 4.0 job roles.
 
• It will be a propagator of vocational education at an early level for youth to capitalize on industry-linked opportunities.
 
• The National Educational Policy 2020 also puts focus on vocational training for holistic growth and increased employability.

questions.question: Loudness of sound is proportional to the ______ of the amplitude of the vibration producing the sound.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Square**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sound is produced by any kind of vibrations. 
 
• As sound waves are longitudinal waves, the air particles vibrate to and fro in the direction of the propagation of sound.
 
• It is a wave of compression and rarefaction.
 
• The amplitude of wavelength is the maximum distance the particle oscillating moves from the mean position.
 
• The frequency of the wave is the number of times one complete cycle of compressions 
 
• 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7bc73a3078186f11a5b5eb735863b0975e3720858151c33bebbb537f8c916141.png] 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The loudness of sound is related to the intensity of sound. 
 
• The loudness is directly proportional to the square of the amplitude. 

L ∝ A2

 
• It has nothing to do with the wavelength and frequency of sound. 
 
• The Pitch of the sound is determined by the frequency.

questions.question: How many players are there in a Field Hockey team?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __11__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Field hockey, also called hockey is an outdoor game played by two opposing teams of 11 players each.
 
• Players use sticks curved at the striking end to hit a small, hard ball into their opponent's goal.
 
• It is called field hockey to distinguish it from the similar game played on ice.
 
• Rules are made by the International Federation of Hockey. 
 
• The total duration of a field hockey match is 60 minutes. 
 
• It is played in four quarters of 15 minutes each.
 
• It consists of a goalkeeper and 10 field players.
 
• There are five substitutes on the bench and there is no limit to the number of times a player is allowed to be substituted.
 
• Apart from the length of the game, there are tied overtime of 5 minutes followed by a shootout.

questions.question: Which of the following fundamental rights implies the prohibition of traffic in human beings, begar and other forms of forced labour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right against Exploitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 23__ deals with the 'Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour'.
 
• Article 23 of the Constitution amended in 2014 includes the following provisions:
 __
 
• Traffic in human beings and begar and other similar forms of forced labour are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.
 
 
 
• The Right against exploitation enshrined in Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution guarantees human dignity and protects people from any exploitation.
 
• Thus, upholding the principles of human dignity and liberty upon which the Indian Constitution is based.
 
• Hence, Article 23 has a very wide scope by ensuring that a person is not forced to do anything involuntarily.
 
• For instance, it forbids a landowner to force a landless, poor labourer to render free services.
 
• It also forbids forcing a woman or child into prostitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

questions.question: Which of the following minerals is responsible for synthesis of thyroxine hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Iodine__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Thyroxin regulates carbohydrate, protein, and fat metabolism in the body to achieve optimal growth balance.
 
• Thyroxine hormone is secreted by the thyroid gland into the bloodstream.
 
• The thyroid gland is the largest endocrine gland.
 
• Thyroxine hormone is an iodinated form of the amino acid (tyrosine).
 
• They are stored in the colloid that fills the follicles and released into the blood when needed.
 
• It then travels to organs such as the liver and kidneys, where it is converted into its active form triiodothyronine.
 
• Iodine (from the diet) is required for the synthesis of thyroxine hormone.
 
• Functions of thyroxine hormone:
 
 
• The thyroid hormone serves several functions in the body, such as
 
• The thyroxine hormone maintains and regulates the Basal Metabolic Rate.
 
• They contribute to the formation of red blood cells.
 
• It also helps in controlling the metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats.
 
• It has an impact on the maintenance of water and electrolytes in our bodies.

questions.question: The Governor of a state is appointed by the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Article 155, The Governor of a State shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• State Governor: Historical Background:
 
 
• The appointment and powers of government can be derived from Part VI of the Indian constitution.
 
• State Governor is appointed by the President of India.
 
• Article 153 says that there shall be a Governor for each State.
 
• One person can be appointed as Governor for two or more States.
 
• The governor acts in 'Dual Capacity' as the Constitutional head of the state and as the representative.
 
• He is part of the federal system of Indian polity and acts as a bridge between union and state governments. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Governors under the Government of India Act 1935 were “by the Raj, of the Raj and for the Raj”.
 
• The constituent assembly wanted elected governors as proposed by a sub-committee of B.G. Kher, K.N. Katju, and P. Subbarayan.
 
• The apprehension of the clash between the powers of Governor and the Chief Minister led to the system of appointed Governors in the state.
 
• The draft constitution of 1948 was ambivalent – the drafting committee leaving it to the constituent assembly to decide whether governors should be elected or nominated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Article 164 states that The **Chief Minister** shall be appointed by the Governor and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.
 
• Advocate General of State:
 
 
• The Constitution (Article 165) has provided for the office of the Advocate General for the States.
 
• He is the highest law officer in the state. Thus he corresponds to the Attorney General of India.
 
• The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor. 
 
 
 
• Article 75 of the Indian Constitution mentions that a** Prime Minister** is appointed by the **President**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The iron materials and furnaces of the iron age are found in Hastinapur and Atranjikheda in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The period between 1200 BC and 600 BC is known as the iron age.
 
• The historic age is also known as the iron age.
 
• This period was known as the iron age because tools and other artefacts were made from iron for the first time.
 
• In this age, painted grey ware and black polished utensils were found.
 
• The evidence of the iron age has been traced from Ahichhhatra, Hastinapur, Mathura, Shravasti, and Kampilya.
 
• Hastinapur is an ancient city that was the capital of the Kuru Empire.
 
 
• The origin of Hastinapur can be traced back to Iron Age.
 
• Items like slag, tuyeres, furnaces, or crucibles were excavated from Hastinapur.
 
 
 
• Ataranji Khera is located in the Etah district of Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
• It belongs to the Kushan period.
 
• Burnt brick structures, terracotta human and animal figurines, beads, iron materials, and furnaces were excavated from Ataranji Khera.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kuru was a Vedic Indo-Aryan tribal confederation that formed in the Middle Vedic period in northern Iron Age India, comprising the modern-day states of Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, and some sections of western Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Panchal was a northern Indian ancient kingdom located in the Ganges-Yamuna Doab of the upper Gangetic plain.
 
 
• It was one of the most powerful nations in Ancient India during the Late Vedic period, closely connected with the Kuru Kingdom.
 
 
 
• Kashi was an ancient Indian kingdom centred in the territory around its capital Varanasi, which was called for the Varuna and Asi rivers in the north and south.
 
 
• It was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.
 
 
 
• Kosal was the kingdom of Treta Yuga's famed figure, Raghava Rama.
 
 
• Its capital was Ayodhya, which is now located in Uttar Pradesh's Ayodhya district.
